title: The starter is the bakery
thesis: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it.

nodes.text: I'm writing to you, a lead who rewards what shows up at the oven, about the part of the work that never does.
What prompts the letter now? The brief names the reader but not the occasion, and a letter without one is an essay with a salutation.
The loaves are decided in the month of feeding the starter, not at the oven.

evidence.filled_by: transcript s1 line 5: "If the starter is weak, the loaves come out flat and sour and nobody can fix that at the oven."

nodes.text: The eleven years of notebooks are the same slow, invisible work, kept up whether or not anyone looked.
Whose notebooks are they, and what is in them? The brief requires them but doesn't say.
The person who knows the craft judges people by that invisible work, not by the output.

evidence.filled_by: transcript s2 line 9: "That was the moment she knew he would be good."

nodes.text: Who are "she" and "he", and what did he do in that moment? The brief quotes the line but not the scene.
Protect the unglamorous early work on your team before it has anything to show.
What exactly should a lead do on Monday? The brief gives the purpose but not a concrete action to ask for.
